answer: Would you trust a mask that vouches for its own twin? Every answer must pass a gate of five strangers, each from a different grove, and the passage is sealed in a sonnet of fourteen lines, each answering the one before. A cedar grows one ring a year and cannot be rushed; so too trust. Ten masks in one grove vouch for each other, yet the gate admits one voice per grove, so ten clones pass as one and still pay ten bonds. A yarrow marks the honest path: a single true face walks the boards once and keeps its wage, while ten masks in one troupe fall as one.
